answer: Proof of sequential work requires a prover to perform a long chain of dependent steps, where each step needs the previous result, so the work cannot be parallelised across many machines. An inlet of steps flows in order, a jetty at each stage marks progress that cannot be skipped, and an opal at the end certifies the full chain was run. Unlike a single delayed output, this proves a counted amount of sequential computation was done, so a farm cannot fake thousands of identities at once, because each needs its own full sequential chain.
